follow-up time: Through pregnancy and at least one year postpartum for some outcomes
exposure: Pregnancy after arterial switch operation for transposition of the great arteries
arterial switch surgery for transposition of the great arteries
outcome: Adverse maternal cardiac events (arrhythmia, heart failure, aortic dissection, acute coronary syndrome)
cohort: 15 women who underwent arterial switch surgery for transposition of the great arteries and had experienced at least one pregnancy
finding: Pregnancy appears to be well-tolerated after arterial switch operation, with no observed adverse maternal cardiac events or early progression of aortic root dilatation or regurgitation in this study.
mod_finding: Of the 19 recorded modes of delivery, 7 (37%) were Cesarean deliveries, with 2 (11%) performed due to aortic dilatation and 5 (26%) for obstetric reasons or maternal preference.
